part 1/2: [doctrine] "wilful ignorance" vs "ignorantia affectata": 'affectata' means 'affected/feigned'; 'wilful' is a weaker, different rendering.

part 1/1: [agency] "He moves them with good desires" vs "Deum quoque affectus nostros... corrigere, & bonis desideriis... afficere": God corrects and affects; 'He moves' obscures that God is agent of both.; [modality] "freer" vs "facilior": 'facilior' means 'easier,' not 'freer'—wrong lexical choice.; [negation] "no longer fight back as much as before" vs "non usque adeo, uti ante, reluctantibus": Ablative absolute 'reluctantibus' means 'with them resisting,' not 'no longer resisting'—negation invented.; [completeness] "since the affections and that law at war in our members no longer fight back" vs "non usque adeo, uti ante, reluctantibus affectibus, & lege illa in membris belligerante": 'non usque adeo' modifies degree of resistance, not temporal 'no longer'—mistranslated construction.

part 1/1: [source_identity] "the will becomes readier, freer and less hindered" vs "promptior & facilior, ac minus impedita": Latin has 'easier' (facilior), not 'freer'; translator substituted a different concept.

part 1/1: [agency] "the Spirit's action on the will has the word's action under it" vs "actionem spiritus... sibi subordinatam habere actionem verbi": Spirit's action has word's action under it reverses subordination: word's action is subordinated to Spirit's action, not vice versa.; [agency] "he works beside the word rather than through it" vs "juxta verbum operari dicamus, non per verbum": Missing subject 'we' (dicamus); 'he works' makes Spirit the subject, but Latin has impersonal/accusative+infinitive construction with 'we say'.; [modality] "who knows what hidden motions" vs "nescio quos arcanos motus": 'Nescio quos' means 'I-know-not what' (indefinite), not 'who knows what'—changes speaker from author to rhetorical question.

part 1/1: [completeness] "Otherwise we may seem to hand the Enthusiasts" vs "ne Enthusiastis doctrinae suae principia": 'ne' is a purpose clause ('lest'); 'Otherwise' misrepresents it as a conditional consequence.

part 1/1: [source_identity] "Greek only" vs "Verum ut clarius adhuc mentem suam explicent": Source is Latin, not Greek as stated in prompt.; [completeness] "working by urging, setting before, inviting" vs "suadendo, proponendo, invitando": Ablative gerunds 'by persuading, by proposing' mistranslated as participles 'working by urging, setting before'—changes grammar and obscures means.; [completeness] "and has a real efficiency of its own" vs "realem ac propriam habere efficientiam": Dropped 'ac propriam' (and proper); 'of its own' is interpretive, not 'propriam' (proper/own).
